title: Drop #3: Feb 15 to 28, 2026
intro: Two more weeks, boiled down. The Supreme Court struck down Trump's tariffs, Paramount beat Netflix for Warner Bros. Discovery, Team USA took Olympic hockey gold twice, and Anthropic and the Pentagon had a showdown.

spotlight.label: One Pikachu card
spotlight.detail: A record sale for a Pokémon card, as the franchise turned 30.

note: Fourteen issues in this drop, one for every day.

issues.label: Issue of Feb 15
issues.top: The big business of little sweet treats

bullets.h: Sunday theme issue: candy, the big business of little sweet treats.
TikTok is fueling a candy craze
bullets.t: Swedish pick-and-mix shops, freeze-dried candy, and 'Dubai chocolate' are all trending. Freeze-dried candy is projected to grow from $1.3 billion in 2024 to $3.1 billion in 2034.

bullets.h: Candy franchises built to last
bullets.t: Candy Crush still had about 180 million players in 2024, the Wonka movies keep earning, and Candy Land sells about a million copies a year.

bullets.h: Mars is really a pet company
bullets.t: The $137 billion business makes about 60% of its revenue from pet care and owns more than 3,000 vet clinics.

bullets.h: Holidays belong to candy
bullets.t: 56% of US shoppers were projected to buy Valentine's candy, and Americans spend $3.3 billion on Easter treats.

bullets.h: Candy in a wellness world
bullets.t: Convenience store candy trips fell 7.5%, GLP-1 drugs are changing cravings, and big brands are phasing out artificial dyes.

issues.label: Issue of Feb 16
issues.top: Warner Bros. Discovery may talk to Paramount again

bullets.h: The Simpsons aired its record-extending 800th episode, after nearly 40 years on the air.
The DHS shutdown drags on
bullets.t: The partial shutdown has no end in sight, since lawmakers don't return to Washington until next week.

bullets.h: US officials speak up at the Munich Security Conference
bullets.t: Marco Rubio urged European nations to 'revitalize an old friendship' with the US.

bullets.h: WBD may reopen talks with Paramount
bullets.t: Paramount sent another sweetened offer on Feb. 10, and some WBD board members wonder if it offers a path to a superior deal.

bullets.h: US men's hockey beats Germany at the Olympics
bullets.t: The win earns a bye to the quarterfinals.

bullets.h: OpenAI hires the OpenClaw founder
bullets.t: Sam Altman scooped up Peter Steinberger, whose open-source AI agents can finish tasks without constant oversight.

bullets.h: 5% to 7%: share of hotel revenue free breakfast can cost
bullets.t: Hyatt Place dropped free breakfast at dozens of hotels, and Holiday Inn went buffet-only.

bullets.h: Denouement
bullets.t: Means 'the final outcome.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 17
issues.top: The Epstein files are toppling business bigwigs

bullets.h: Happy Lunar New Year and Mardi Gras. The Snake is out, and the Fire Horse gallops in.
The Epstein files shake up boardrooms
bullets.t: Hyatt's Tom Pritzker is leaving the board and Goldman's top lawyer Kathryn Ruemmler resigned. Casey Wasserman is selling his talent agency.

bullets.h: Actor Robert Duvall dies at 95
bullets.t: Star of The Godfather and Apocalypse Now, he won Best Actor for Tender Mercies.

bullets.h: US women's hockey beats Sweden 5 to 0
bullets.t: They advance to the gold medal game against Canada.

bullets.h: The Pentagon is 'close' to cutting ties with Anthropic
bullets.t: A dispute over military use of Claude could get Anthropic labeled a supply chain risk.

bullets.h: ByteDance adds AI safeguards after Disney's threat
bullets.t: Its Seedance 2.0 video tool was accused of using studios' characters without permission.

bullets.h: KPMG partner fined for using AI on an AI test
bullets.t: The unnamed partner paid $7,000 and had to retake the exam.

bullets.h: Maxxing and mogging, decoded
bullets.t: 'Maxxing' means optimizing for whatever you attach it to, like looksmaxxing. 'Mogging' means one-upping someone, the end goal of maxxing.

bullets.h: 1 in 9: CEOs replaced last year
bullets.t: That's the highest turnover since 2010, and companies worth $2.2 trillion have already changed leaders in 2026.

bullets.h: Potpourri
bullets.t: Means 'a mixture of things.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 18
issues.top: Rent control is the talk of Boston

bullets.h: Happy Pluto Day. It was discovered on Feb. 18, 1930, then demoted to dwarf planet in 2006.
Civil rights leader Rev. Jesse Jackson dies at 84
bullets.t: He founded the Rainbow PUSH Coalition and ran for president twice.

bullets.h: Paramount gets another shot at WBD
bullets.t: Netflix gave WBD a seven-day waiver to reopen talks, and Paramount's offer includes covering the $2.8 billion fee owed to Netflix.

bullets.h: Colbert says CBS blocked an interview over FCC concerns
bullets.t: CBS says it only gave legal guidance.

bullets.h: Tide launches waterless detergent tiles
bullets.t: Tide evo dissolves in cold water. A box of 42 costs $19.99 on Amazon versus $12.97 for Pods.

bullets.h: Massachusetts may vote on rent control
bullets.t: A November ballot question would cap rent hikes at inflation, up to 5%. Gov. Maura Healey opposes it.

bullets.h: 2x: how much more often startups work from home
bullets.t: Employees at companies founded after 2015 work from home nearly twice as often as those at companies founded before 1990.

bullets.h: Conundrum
bullets.t: Means 'an intricate and difficult problem.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 19
issues.top: Zuck testifies at a landmark social media trial

bullets.h: A runaway local dog crashed the Olympic women's cross-country sprint and crossed the finish line to cheers.
Fed minutes: rate cuts are likely months away
bullets.t: Officials are divided on what should trigger a cut, and proof of lower inflation is unlikely for months.

bullets.h: US masses its most airpower in the Mideast since 2003
bullets.t: Strikes on Iran could come as soon as this weekend, while talks continue.

bullets.h: eBay to buy Depop from Etsy
bullets.t: The cash deal is worth about $1.2 billion.

bullets.h: The Seahawks are up for sale
bullets.t: The Super Bowl champs could fetch up to $8 billion, an NFL record.

bullets.h: Mikaela Shiffrin wins slalom gold
bullets.t: It's her first Olympic win in eight years.

bullets.h: Zuckerberg testifies in a landmark trial
bullets.t: It's the first time he's answered claims that Instagram harms kids in front of a jury. The case could shape thousands of similar lawsuits.

bullets.h: A robot dog gets a school kicked out of India's AI summit
bullets.t: A professor passed off a commercially available Chinese robot dog as her university's own creation.

bullets.h: 55 seats: JPMorgan's staff pub for about 10,000 workers
bullets.t: Reservations at Morgan's are so hot that younger staffers book weeks out.

bullets.h: Bellwether
bullets.t: Means 'one that takes the lead or initiative.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 20
issues.top: Trade deficit barely budges despite Trump's tariffs

bullets.h: Punch, a baby monkey at a Japanese zoo, went viral cuddling a plush orangutan, and now the other monkeys hang with him.
The trade deficit barely budges despite tariffs
bullets.t: It fell just 0.2% to $901.5 billion in 2025. The deficit with China shrank, but it grew with Taiwan, Mexico, and Vietnam.

bullets.h: Walmart posts strong sales but a cautious outlook
bullets.t: Holiday sales rose 6%, and Amazon passed Walmart in annual sales, $717 billion to $713.2 billion.

bullets.h: Former Prince Andrew is arrested
bullets.t: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor was held on suspicion of misconduct in public office tied to Epstein, the first arrest of a senior British royal since 1647.

bullets.h: Trump commits $10 billion to his 'Board of Peace'
bullets.t: He didn't say where the money would come from, and many US allies declined to join.

bullets.h: Actor Eric Dane dies at 53
bullets.t: Best known as Dr. McSteamy on Grey's Anatomy, he died 10 months after announcing his ALS diagnosis.

bullets.h: Nestlé plans to sell its ice cream brands
bullets.t: It's in advanced talks to sell to Froneri, a joint venture it created, to focus on coffee, pet care, and snacks.

bullets.h: US women's hockey wins Olympic gold
bullets.t: They beat Canada 2 to 1 in overtime. Alysa Liu also won figure skating gold, the first American to do so since 2002.

bullets.h: $3,400: what some top lawyers charge per hour
bullets.t: That's up from $2,500 a year ago, and partner rates at big firms rose 16% last year.

bullets.h: Excoriated
bullets.t: Means 'censured or criticized severely.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 21
issues.top: The Supreme Court struck down Trump's tariffs

bullets.h: The USA faces Canada in the men's Olympic hockey gold medal game tomorrow. Stock up on beer, bacon, and more Katy Perry than expected.
The Supreme Court rules Trump's global tariffs illegal
bullets.t: In a 6 to 3 decision, the court said he overstepped his authority. Trump announced a new 10% global tariff under a different law, and refunds could reach $175 billion.

bullets.h: Blue Owl's $1.4 billion asset sale rattles private credit
bullets.t: Its shares fell about 12%, and Blackstone, KKR, and Apollo also slipped.

bullets.h: US growth slowed to 1.4% at the end of 2025
bullets.t: That's down from 4.4% the quarter before, partly because of the shutdown.

bullets.h: Trump says he's considering limited strikes on Iran
bullets.t: Iran says it will send a proposed deal within days.

bullets.h: Trump orders release of government UFO files
bullets.t: The Pentagon and other agencies are to release files on aliens and unidentified aerial phenomena.

bullets.h: Miley Cyrus is back at the beach house for a Hannah Montana 20th anniversary special
A Chicago man jumped into freezing Lake Michigan to save a baby in a stroller blown into the water
A sleeper shark was spotted swimming in the near-freezing waters of Antarctica
Sam Altman and Dario Amodei avoided holding hands at India's AI summit photo op
Shenanigans
bullets.t: Means 'high-spirited or mischievous activity.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 22
issues.top: What's owned by private equity and what will be soon

bullets.h: Sunday theme issue: private equity, from your dentist to your fonts.
Is private equity past its prime?
bullets.t: PE owns almost 13,000 US companies, about 7% of GDP, but returns trail the S&P 500: 5.8% versus 11.6% a year from 2022 to Q3 2025.

bullets.h: PE loves restaurants
bullets.t: It invested $94.5 billion in bars and restaurants from 2014 to 2024. McAlister's thrived, but nearly half of 2024 restaurant bankruptcies were PE-backed.

bullets.h: The human cost in healthcare
bullets.t: A Harvard-coauthored study found a 13% rise in emergency department deaths at hospitals after PE acquisitions.

bullets.h: PE is coming for sports
bullets.t: 74 major US pro teams have PE ties, including 20 of 30 NBA teams. The Patriots were the first PE-backed team in a Super Bowl.

bullets.h: What else PE owns
bullets.t: Font library Monotype, big music catalogs, and YouTube channels like Cocomelon.

issues.label: Issue of Feb 23
issues.top: Businesses face an uphill climb on tariff refunds

bullets.h: Team USA beat Canada in overtime for men's hockey gold, 46 years to the day after the Miracle on Ice. Proposed nickname: The United Skates of America.
Companies face an uphill climb for tariff refunds
bullets.t: The court left the process to the Court of International Trade. Hundreds of firms, including Costco and Dole, have sued, and Trump says it could take five years.

bullets.h: Bitcoin falls below $65,000
bullets.t: Renewed global trade tensions weighed on crypto.

bullets.h: A Nor'easter blankets the Northeast
bullets.t: Six states declared emergencies, and New York City banned road travel overnight.

bullets.h: Mexico's army kills cartel leader El Mencho
bullets.t: The Jalisco cartel boss died after a raid, sparking violence in almost a dozen states.

bullets.h: One Battle After Another wins best film at the BAFTAs
Axe redesigns its body spray to cut the fog
bullets.t: New cans are lighter and hold 10% more sprays. Its US share of deodorant sprays fell from 24% to 16.3%.

bullets.h: 12: gold medals for Team USA
bullets.t: It also took a record 33 total medals, the most ever at a Winter Olympics.

bullets.h: Wield
bullets.t: Means 'to handle effectively.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 24
issues.top: Pentagon and Anthropic chiefs meet amid beef

bullets.h: The State of the Union is tonight. Place your bets on the length: last year's address ran 1 hour and 39 minutes.
FedEx sues for a full tariff refund
bullets.t: It looks to be the first large US company to sue after the Supreme Court ruling.

bullets.h: A huge snowstorm hits 40 million people
bullets.t: Parts of New York City got 19 inches, and Providence broke its record with 32.8 inches.

bullets.h: Pentagon concerned about a long Iran campaign
bullets.t: The Wall Street Journal says military leaders raised worries to Trump.

bullets.h: Mortgage rates fall below 6%
bullets.t: The 30-year fixed rate hit 5.99%, the lowest since 2022, and refinance applications are up 130% from a year ago.

bullets.h: Gen Z is picking up iPods
bullets.t: Searches for the iPod Classic rose 25% last year, and downloads of the phone-blocking Brick app were up about 600% in January.

bullets.h: Anthropic's CEO meets the Pentagon to save a $200 million deal
bullets.t: They disagree on whether Claude can be used for surveillance of Americans or fully autonomous weapons. Hegseth has floated a 'supply chain risk' label.

bullets.h: 10%: drop in AMC attendance last year
bullets.t: It cut its losses, and expects a better 2026 slate with films like The Odyssey.

bullets.h: Cinephiles
bullets.t: Means 'film enthusiasts.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 25
issues.top: Trump gives a record-long State of the Union

bullets.h: The cottage from Heated Rivalry is now on Airbnb, with a fire pit and 400 feet of private waterfront.
Jamie Dimon's 'anxiety is high'
bullets.t: The JPMorgan CEO says the current climate reminds him of the run-up to 2008, with lenders making risky bets.

bullets.h: Novo Nordisk slashes Ozempic and Wegovy prices
bullets.t: From 2027 each lists at $675 a month, cuts of 34% and 50%.

bullets.h: Trump delivers a record 108-minute State of the Union
bullets.t: He defended his tariffs and declared a 'War on Fraud.' Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger gave the Democratic response, focused on affordability.

bullets.h: Dark Sky's creators launch Acme Weather
bullets.t: It shows several possible forecasts and community-reported conditions, even rainbows, for $25 a year.

bullets.h: AMD signs a $100 billion chip deal with Meta
bullets.t: Meta will buy 6 gigawatts of AI chips and can own up to 10% of AMD.

bullets.h: 54%: US teens using AI chatbots for schoolwork
bullets.t: 59% think cheating with AI happens regularly at their school.

bullets.h: Oblate
bullets.t: Means 'round but flattened at the top and bottom.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 26
issues.top: Nvidia profits boom, investors shrug

bullets.h: Meteorological spring starts March 1 and astronomical spring starts March 20, so real spring is whenever you hear the first sneeze.
Kalshi fines a MrBeast video editor for insider trading
bullets.t: He paid over $20,000 and was suspended for two years for trading on markets tied to MrBeast videos.

bullets.h: US and Iran talk in Geneva
bullets.t: The US says any deal must include Iran giving up its nuclear program.

bullets.h: Bill Gates apologizes and Larry Summers resigns over Epstein ties
bullets.t: Summers is stepping down from his teaching roles at Harvard.

bullets.h: Survivor kicks off its 50th season
bullets.t: Last year it was the most-watched Emmy nominee, with 462.4 million viewing hours.

bullets.h: Nvidia posts record sales, but investors shrug
bullets.t: Q4 sales hit $68.1 billion, up 73%, and it forecasts about $78 billion next quarter.

bullets.h: Anthropic drops a core safety pledge
bullets.t: It will no longer pause training if a model outpaces its safeguards, unless it has a significant lead.

bullets.h: $5.84: the average tooth fairy payout
bullets.t: That's up 17% from 2025, and a first tooth now fetches $7.17.

bullets.h: Astronomical
bullets.t: Means 'of or relating to astronomy.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 27
issues.top: Paramount wins the WBD bidding war

bullets.h: Tampa's airport wants a jammy-free zone after a 'crisis' of people flying in pajamas.
Pakistan declares 'open war' on Afghanistan
bullets.t: It followed overnight cross-border attacks.

bullets.h: US and Iran leave talks without a deal
bullets.t: Mediators still reported significant progress.

bullets.h: Paramount beats Netflix for Warner Bros. Discovery
bullets.t: Its $31 per share offer, about $111 billion, won after Netflix refused to raise its bid. Netflix gets a $2.8 billion breakup fee.

bullets.h: Burger King tests an AI headset coach named Patty
bullets.t: It listens for 'please' and 'thank you' to grade friendliness. The chain also says it will finally improve the Whopper.

bullets.h: Papa Johns will close 300 stores
bullets.t: Interest in pizza is waning.

bullets.h: Stellantis posts its first annual loss ever
bullets.t: It followed the company scaling back its EV strategy.

bullets.h: Instagram will alert parents to suicide-related teen searches
bullets.t: Alerts apply to teens and parents who enroll.

bullets.h: Anthropic says it 'cannot in good conscience' meet Pentagon demands
bullets.t: It wants guarantees Claude won't be used for mass surveillance or fully autonomous weapons.

bullets.h: Block will cut about 40% of staff in an AI pivot
bullets.t: Headcount drops from over 10,000 to just under 6,000, and the stock rose 24% after hours.

bullets.h: 63%: trust in banks in crisis-hit countries
bullets.t: It's up from 40% in 2009, and higher than trust in governments or courts.

bullets.h: Homilies
bullets.t: Means 'sermons that interpret scripture.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 28
issues.top: Anthropic blacklisted as OpenAI gets the Pentagon deal

bullets.h: It's the last day of February, which was cut to 28 days thanks to ancient Roman superstitions about even numbers.
US evacuates some embassy staff as Iran talks stall
bullets.t: Trump says he's 'not happy' with Iran and hasn't decided on an attack.

bullets.h: Bill Clinton says he 'saw nothing' in his Epstein deposition
bullets.t: He sat for an hourslong closed-door session with a House committee.

bullets.h: Pokémon turns 30
bullets.t: It has earned about $150 billion, and a Pikachu Illustrator card sold for a record $16.5 million.

bullets.h: Pop hitmaker Neil Sedaka dies at 86
bullets.t: He wrote 'Breaking Up Is Hard to Do' and 'Calendar Girl.'

bullets.h: OpenAI lands the Pentagon deal after Anthropic is blacklisted
bullets.t: Trump ordered agencies to stop using Anthropic, and the Pentagon labeled it a supply chain risk. Hours later OpenAI announced a classified-network deal with similar guardrails.

bullets.h: OpenAI raises $110 billion
bullets.t: Amazon puts in $50 billion, and Nvidia and SoftBank $30 billion each, at a $730 billion valuation before the new money.

bullets.h: An Australian supermarket's AI chatbot apologized for telling stories about its mother
A Florida nudist camp is for sale for $2.5 million
Researchers say the origins of writing go back tens of thousands of years further than thought
A serial stowaway was arrested again for sneaking onto a Newark to Milan flight
Soiree
bullets.t: Means 'a party held in the evening.'

title: Drop #2: Feb 1 to 14, 2026
intro: Two more weeks, boiled down. Big Tech's AI spending plans topped $650 billion, bitcoin sank below $70,000, Disney picked a new CEO, and the Seahawks won Super Bowl LX.

spotlight.label: Super Bowls attended
spotlight.detail: Three lifelong fans have been to every single one, since 1967 when a ticket cost $12.

note: Fourteen issues in this drop, one for every day.

issues.label: Issue of Feb 1
issues.top: The business of sports fandom is changing

bullets.h: Sunday theme issue: the business of sports fandom, from jerseys to stadium hot dogs.
Fanatics wants to be your whole fan life
bullets.t: The merch giant brought in about $13 billion last year and wants to hit $50 billion. Its betting arm doubled to about 8% market share, and a branded credit card arrives this spring.

bullets.h: That ticket might not be yours to sell
bullets.t: Teams use digital-only tickets, price floors, and fines to limit resale. The NFL fined more than 100 players and staff for flipping Super Bowl tickets last year.

bullets.h: Stadium food is getting cheaper
bullets.t: After Atlanta cut hot dogs from $8 to $2, transactions jumped 30%. Utah, Phoenix, and Baltimore followed, though one Commanders beer still cost $16.49.

bullets.h: Pop culture is minting new fans
bullets.t: Hockey ticket interest on StubHub spiked 40% during the hit show Heated Rivalry, and Taylor Swift tripled Chiefs home ticket sales on StubHub.

bullets.h: Free stuff fills seats
bullets.t: Bobbleheads, jerseys, and quirky giveaways keep stands full, especially in baseball. The Panthers once offered a lifetime supply of mayo for every forced turnover.

issues.label: Issue of Feb 2
issues.top: AI agents get their own social network

bullets.h: It's Groundhog Day. Phil's overall forecast accuracy is about 35%, so we'll take the over.
Bitcoin slips below $76,000
bullets.t: That's about 40% off its October high, after a fourth straight losing month.

bullets.h: Shutdown fix in sight, maybe
bullets.t: House Speaker Mike Johnson says the partial shutdown will end by Tuesday, but the House margins are razor thin.

bullets.h: Kendrick Lamar and Bad Bunny sweep the Grammys
bullets.t: Kendrick won five, bringing his total to 27, the most ever for a rapper. Bad Bunny took album of the year, and Trevor Noah hosted for the sixth and final time.

bullets.h: Walmart and Target get new CEOs
bullets.t: John Furner takes over a thriving Walmart, while Michael Fiddelke inherits a Target with 10 of the last 12 quarters flat or down.

bullets.h: Alcaraz wins the Australian Open
bullets.t: He beat Djokovic and became the youngest player to complete a career Grand Slam.

bullets.h: Moltbook mania: hilarity or singularity?
bullets.t: A Reddit-style site where only AI agents post claimed 1.5 million users and an AI religion called Crustafarianism. Musk called it the early stages of the singularity, while skeptics say many posts are fake.

bullets.h: 28: days of calendar perfection
bullets.t: February starts on a Sunday and ends on a Saturday, a perfect four-week grid. The last time was 2015, and the next is 2037.

bullets.h: Thaumaturgy
bullets.t: Means 'magic' or 'miracle-working.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 3
issues.top: Musk merges SpaceX and xAI

bullets.h: Phil saw his shadow, so it's six more weeks of winter, and the crowd booed him.
The US and India strike a trade deal
bullets.t: US tariffs on Indian goods drop to 18%, and India agrees to stop buying Russian oil.

bullets.h: Project Vault: a $12 billion minerals stockpile
bullets.t: The US is stashing rare earths and critical minerals, about 60 days' worth, to loosen China's grip on supply.

bullets.h: Disney's next CEO may come from the parks
bullets.t: Parks chief Josh D'Amaro is the favorite, helped by a record $10 billion quarterly profit from parks and cruises.

bullets.h: Crying horse replaces Labubu
bullets.t: A $3.60 plush horse with an upside-down snout went viral, and about 15,000 are ordered daily.

bullets.h: Musk merges SpaceX and xAI
bullets.t: The deal values the combined company at about $1.25 trillion, and Musk is pitching data centers in space.

bullets.h: 393,812: minivans sold last year, up 21%
bullets.t: Overall car sales grew just 2%. Dads in their forties are driving the comeback.

bullets.h: Tchotchke
bullets.t: Means 'a knickknack.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 4
issues.top: PayPal's stock tanks as it replaces its CEO

bullets.h: A new study says rocking yourself to sleep helps you nod off faster and remember more. Guess we're all babies now.
PayPal swaps its CEO and the stock tanks
bullets.t: Enrique Lores replaces Alex Chriss on March 1. Weak guidance sent shares down more than 20%, and the stock has lost nearly half its value in a year.

bullets.h: The House ends the partial shutdown
bullets.t: A $1.2 trillion funding bill passed, but Homeland Security is only funded through Feb. 13.

bullets.h: Disney taps parks boss Josh D'Amaro as CEO
bullets.t: He replaces Bob Iger on March 18, so for the first time since 2005 Disney's CEO won't be named Bob.

bullets.h: PepsiCo cuts snack prices up to 15%
bullets.t: Doritos and friends get cheaper as shoppers pinch pennies, with no shrinkflation.

bullets.h: Rome's Trevi Fountain now costs 2 euros
bullets.t: It's free after 10pm, and locals are exempt.

bullets.h: Spain bans social media for under-16s
bullets.t: It's the first European country to do it, joining Australia, and France is considering the same.

bullets.h: $1 trillion: Walmart's market value
bullets.t: Only the 11th company to reach the club, and the first traditional retailer.

bullets.h: Dissemination
bullets.t: Means 'the act of spreading something widely.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 5
issues.top: How AI tanked software stocks

bullets.h: Nancy Meyers is back with her first movie in 11 years, due Christmas 2027 on a $150 million budget.
The last US-Russia nuclear treaty expires
bullets.t: New START ends, raising fears of a fresh arms race.

bullets.h: Nike faces a federal discrimination probe
bullets.t: The EEOC is looking at whether its diversity goals led to unfair treatment of white employees.

bullets.h: The Washington Post lays off 30% of its staff
bullets.t: More than 300 of 800 journalists are cut, shrinking international coverage and nearly erasing the sports desk.

bullets.h: McDonald's drops a free McNugget Caviar kit
bullets.t: It includes a $25 gift card and a tin of caviar, and it launches online Feb. 10.

bullets.h: AI's latest victim: software stocks
bullets.t: A new Anthropic legal tool for its Cowork assistant helped wipe almost $300 billion off software stocks in a day. Investors fear AI could replace many software products.

bullets.h: Alphabet plans $185 billion in AI spending
bullets.t: That's double last year, on top of record sales of $403 billion in 2025.

bullets.h: 80: years of canned frozen juice
bullets.t: Minute Maid is discontinuing its frozen concentrates after eight decades. The idea began with a 1945 Army order for 500,000 pounds of orange juice.

bullets.h: Tubular
bullets.t: Means 'having the form of a tube.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 6
issues.top: Yesterday might have been crypto's Black Thursday

bullets.h: The Super Bowl is two days away. Party prep: pre-watch the commercials and buy everyone bibs.
Bitcoin falls below $70,000
bullets.t: It dropped as much as 10% in a day and is nearly half off its October peak.

bullets.h: Amazon plans $200 billion in AI spending
bullets.t: That's far more than analysts expected, and the stock fell 10% after hours.

bullets.h: Bob's Discount Furniture goes public
bullets.t: It raised $331 million and was valued at about $2.4 billion.

bullets.h: OpenAI and Anthropic spar over a Super Bowl ad
bullets.t: Anthropic's spots mock ads inside chatbots, and Sam Altman called them dishonest.

bullets.h: The Winter Olympics open today in Italy
bullets.t: NHL players return for the first time since 2014, and Lindsey Vonn is racing on a torn ACL. Gold and silver medals are worth more than double Paris because of metal prices.

bullets.h: 108,435: jobs cut in January
bullets.t: The most for any January since 2009, up 118% from a year ago.

bullets.h: Clarion
bullets.t: Means 'loud and clear.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 7
issues.top: Big Tech's $650 billion AI spending plans

bullets.h: Backup excuses for calling out after the Super Bowl include 'my blood is 40% queso.' About 26 million people are projected to skip Monday.
Big Tech will spend $650 billion on AI this year
bullets.t: Amazon plans $200 billion, Alphabet $185 billion, Meta up to $135 billion, and Microsoft about $105 billion. That's 60% more than last year.

bullets.h: Stellantis takes a $26 billion hit for its EV pivot
bullets.t: Its stock fell about 27%, and Ford and GM also took big charges.

bullets.h: AI is the MVP of Super Bowl ads
bullets.t: Anthropic, Google, Amazon, and Meta all ran spots, weight loss drugs and celebrities were everywhere, and Guy Fieri pitched power tools.

bullets.h: The Winter Olympics open in Milan
bullets.t: The torch was lit in two places for the first time, and Mariah Carey sang 'Volare.'

bullets.h: A Michelangelo drawing of a foot sold for $27.2 million
The Louvre says its stolen crown was found crushed but nearly intact
A wildlife photo finalist shows a deer with another deer's head stuck in its antlers
The Hollywood Reporter asked whether underwear is the new tequila
Emblazoned
bullets.t: Means 'adorned with.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 8
issues.top: If you file on time, that might be too late

bullets.h: Sunday theme issue: taxes. Tax season and the Super Bowl both have hikes, cuts, and game-changing returns.
Mailing your return on April 15? It may be late
bullets.t: The post office is picking up mail less often, so postmarks can land a day late. Try a manual postmark, a courier, or e-filing.

bullets.h: Do tax hikes scare off millionaires?
bullets.t: The evidence is mixed. Massachusetts raised almost $6 billion from its millionaire tax in two years, while some tycoons left California and others stayed.

bullets.h: Athletes chase states with no income tax
bullets.t: Tyreek Hill said 'those state taxes, man,' and saved about $9 million by signing in Florida. Mikko Rantanen's Texas deal is worth about $4 million more.

bullets.h: A side hustle tax tip
bullets.t: Track every expense all year in a simple spreadsheet, match costs to tax categories, and hire a pro once you get more than two forms.

bullets.h: Famous tax troubles
bullets.t: Willie Nelson, Floyd Mayweather, and Al Capone all tangled with the taxman. Nelson even released an album to repay the IRS.

issues.label: Issue of Feb 9
issues.top: Seahawks win Super Bowl LX

bullets.h: The day after the Super Bowl is rough, but luckily we all got decent sleep during the game.
Japan's PM wins big in snap elections
bullets.t: Sanae Takaichi's party and its partner won overwhelming control of the lower house, which she calls a mandate for more defense spending.

bullets.h: Jimmy Lai sentenced to 20 years
bullets.t: The Hong Kong media mogul and pro-democracy advocate got a 20-year prison term.

bullets.h: Washington Post CEO Will Lewis steps down
bullets.t: It comes days after layoffs hit nearly a third of staff. CFO Jeff D'Onofrio is acting CEO.

bullets.h: Glass is the surprise AI winner
bullets.t: Corning stock is up more than 130% in a year after a $6 billion fiber-optic deal with Meta.

bullets.h: Seahawks beat the Patriots 29 to 13 in Super Bowl LX
bullets.t: Bad Bunny's halftime show celebrated Puerto Rico with Lady Gaga and Ricky Martin, and Charlie Puth nailed the anthem.

bullets.h: Team USA wins figure skating team gold
bullets.t: Madison Chock, Evan Bates, and 'Quad God' Ilia Malinin led the way.

bullets.h: 60: Super Bowls attended by three lifelong fans
bullets.t: Tom Henschel, Don Crisman, and Gregory Eaton have been to every one since 1967, when tickets cost $12.

bullets.h: Mandate
bullets.t: Means 'a command to act.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 10
issues.top: Alphabet goes for a 100-year bond

bullets.h: Alphabet to sell 100-year bonds
bullets.t: It raised $20 billion in US bonds to help pay for about $185 billion of AI spending this year.

bullets.h: UK PM Starmer faces calls to resign
bullets.t: The backlash is over an ambassador pick with close Epstein ties. Two top aides have quit, but Starmer says he is staying.

bullets.h: Cuba runs out of jet fuel
bullets.t: Air Canada suspended all flights as US pressure squeezes the island's oil supply.

bullets.h: Ice dance goes 90s
bullets.t: Skaters used Spice Girls and Madonna tracks in the rhythm dance, and one Czech team skated to an AI-made song.

bullets.h: 8.6 years: how long homeowners now stay put
bullets.t: That's the longest on record since 2000, when it was 4.2 years.

bullets.h: Bonanzas
bullets.t: Means 'very large amounts.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 11
issues.top: Trump administration ditches a key climate rule

bullets.h: Two to three cups of coffee a day may lower dementia risk. It may also raise your odds of a bathroom emergency during a 10am meeting.
Ford reports an $8 billion loss
bullets.t: EV charges and a surprisingly large tariff bill drove last year's loss.

bullets.h: The EPA scraps its key climate rule
bullets.t: It's dropping the 2009 endangerment finding, billed as the largest deregulation in US history. Lawsuits are expected.

bullets.h: FBI releases footage in the Nancy Guthrie case
bullets.t: Images show a masked person at the door camera of the Today host's mother. No suspects have been named.

bullets.h: Paramount sweetens its Warner Bros. Discovery bid
bullets.t: It offered to cover a $2.8 billion termination fee if the Netflix deal falls through.

bullets.h: Spotify adds a record 38 million listeners
bullets.t: The stock jumped 15% on 751 million monthly users, with a big boost from Wrapped.

bullets.h: Ferrari shows off its first EV interior
bullets.t: The Luce was designed with Jony Ive's firm and keeps satisfyingly clicky physical controls.

bullets.h: Super Bowl LX draws 124.9 million viewers
bullets.t: The second-biggest audience ever, behind last year's 127.7 million.

bullets.h: 60%: share of new Dollar Tree customers earning six figures
bullets.t: Nearly half of its new stores in six years opened in wealthy areas.

bullets.h: Oxymoron
bullets.t: Means 'a figure of speech with seemingly contradictory terms.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 12
issues.top: It wasn't a dry January for the job market

bullets.h: Rebecca Black's 'Friday' turns 15 this week, with more than 178 million views and counting.
Jobs report beats expectations
bullets.t: The US added 130,000 jobs in January and unemployment fell to 4.3%. Healthcare added 82,000.

bullets.h: Kraft Heinz pauses its breakup
bullets.t: The new CEO says the problems are fixable and plans to invest $600 million instead.

bullets.h: Bill Ackman buys $2 billion of Meta
bullets.t: A bet on the Facebook parent's place in the AI race.

bullets.h: Bondi clashes with lawmakers over the Epstein files
bullets.t: A five-hour hearing got tense, and she did not apologize to survivors in the room.

bullets.h: Switzerland will vote on a population cap
bullets.t: A June referendum would cap the population at 10 million.

bullets.h: Actor James Van Der Beek dies at 48
bullets.t: Known for Dawson's Creek, he shared his colorectal cancer diagnosis in 2024.

bullets.h: Britney Spears sells her music catalog
Doorbell cams spark surveillance fears
bullets.t: The FBI pulled Nest footage from an offline camera, and Ring's Super Bowl dog-finding ad raised alarms.

bullets.h: Leviathan
bullets.t: Means 'something large or formidable.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 13
issues.top: Trump admin ends its immigration crackdown in Minnesota

bullets.h: It's Friday the 13th, and 2/13/26 is a 'magic date' because 2 times 13 equals 26.
Minnesota immigration surge ends
bullets.t: The operation led to more than 4,000 arrests, mass protests, and the deaths of two US citizens. A small team stays behind.

bullets.h: The DOJ antitrust chief resigns
bullets.t: Gail Slater was reportedly pushed out after months of clashes with leadership.

bullets.h: The EPA formally repeals its climate finding
bullets.t: Environmental groups plan to sue, and the Supreme Court may have the last word.

bullets.h: Hilary Duff announces her first world tour in nearly 20 years
Home sales fall 8.4%
bullets.t: Existing-home sales dropped in January, the worst month for closings in more than two years.

bullets.h: Olympic drones steal the show
bullets.t: More than two dozen drones film luge and skiing, but athletes and viewers are bothered by the whirring.

bullets.h: Apple may delay its Siri upgrades
bullets.t: Bloomberg says testing issues could push the planned changes back.

bullets.h: 22%: how much ground beef prices rose in two years
bullets.t: Boneless chicken prices fell 1.7%, so dark meat is in demand.

bullets.h: Volition
bullets.t: Means 'the power to make your own decisions.'

issues.label: Issue of Feb 14
issues.top: Inflation is finally taking a chill pill

bullets.h: Happy Valentine's Day. Roses are red, violets are blue, and we love you, too.
Inflation cools to 2.4%
bullets.t: Prices rose 0.2% in January. Gas fell 3.2% and eggs dropped 7%, but airfare jumped 6.5%.

bullets.h: Homeland Security shuts down over the ICE fight
bullets.t: Funding lapsed as Democrats push for limits on ICE. TSA and Coast Guard staff could miss paychecks if it drags on.

bullets.h: Dubai port boss quits over Epstein ties
bullets.t: DP World's CEO resigned after emails with Epstein came out.

bullets.h: Quad God takes two falls
bullets.t: Ilia Malinin fell twice in his free skate and is out of medal contention.

bullets.h: Ring drops its Flock Safety partnership
bullets.t: The split follows backlash over its Super Bowl ad.

bullets.h: Hollywood vs. the fake Cruise and Pitt fight
bullets.t: A viral AI clip made with ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 drew copyright complaints from the film studios' trade group and SAG-AFTRA.

bullets.h: A Manhattan restaurant now lets diners bring an AI companion as a date
A Stanford student is using an algorithm to pair 5,000 singles
A Slovak fugitive was arrested at an Olympic hockey game
Nick Castellanos says he was benched for bringing a beer into the dugout
Deceleration
bullets.t: Means 'reduction in speed or rate.'

title: Drop #1: Jan 18 to 31, 2026
intro: Two weeks of headlines, boiled down. Greenland tariff threats whipsawed markets, gold blew past $5,000, TikTok went American and then got messy, and Trump named Kevin Warsh as the next Fed chair.

spotlight.label: Seconds to midnight
spotlight.detail: The Doomsday Clock has never been this close.

note: Twelve issues in this drop. Issues for Jan 25 and Jan 26 were not available.

issues.label: Issue of Jan 18
issues.top: Watches are having their finest hour

bullets.h: Sunday theme issue: watches, from the White Rabbit's pocketwatch to James Bond's Omega.
Watches are in their finest hour
bullets.t: Gen Z is shopping secondhand and following watch influencers. The used-watch market hit $27 billion in 2023, and only a few models, like the Rolex Daytona and GMT, still trade at a big premium.

bullets.h: Trends that make your wrist stand out
bullets.t: Odd shapes (a padlock, a bathroom scale, a panther), retro vintage pieces, sustainable materials, and bold colors like avocado and candy pink.

bullets.h: Is watchmaking the next hot career?
bullets.t: Only nine full-time watchmaking schools remain in the US. Rolex runs a tuition-free 18-month program with a $1,800 monthly stipend.

bullets.h: Microbrands' time to shine
bullets.t: Rolex retail prices jumped 18% in two years, while microbrands like Baltic, Serica, and Formex price in the hundreds and low thousands. The microbrand market is expected to grow 25% in five years.

bullets.h: The race to put a doctor on your wrist
bullets.t: Smartwatches have pivoted from step counting to health. Apple added an ECG, then sleep apnea and hypertension alerts. Blood sugar is the next frontier, but no smartwatch can measure it yet. And no federal law stops wearable makers from selling your data.

issues.label: Issue of Jan 19
issues.top: Trump announces new tariffs over Greenland rift

bullets.h: It's MLK Day, the only federal holiday that's also a National Day of Service. US markets were closed.
Trump announces new tariffs over Greenland rift
bullets.t: A 10% tariff on eight European countries is set for Feb. 1, and the EU is weighing up to $108 billion in retaliation.

bullets.h: At least 21 killed in Spain train collision
bullets.t: A high-speed passenger train went off the rails near Córdoba and hit a train coming the other way.

bullets.h: Gaza Board of Peace plan floats $1 billion membership
bullets.t: Member states would serve three-year terms, or pay $1 billion in year one for a permanent seat.

bullets.h: K-food is booming around the world
bullets.t: Korean food exports hit a record $13.6 billion in 2025, and instant noodles jumped nearly 22%.

bullets.h: College football knows how to protect the pocket
bullets.t: Top-division program values are up 46% since last year, and some teams are worth over $1.5 billion. NCAA rule changes allow free transfers and let schools pay athletes up to $20.5 million a year. Indiana's value jumped nearly 68%.

bullets.h: 20%: how much smaller wedding parties are than in 2019
bullets.t: About eight people now versus ten. One writer says seven years of bridesmaid duty cost her nearly $20,000.

bullets.h: Foment
bullets.t: Means 'to promote.'

issues.label: Issue of Jan 20
issues.top: Trump says he'll sue JPMorgan over 'debanking'

bullets.h: Matt Damon says Netflix wants a big action scene in the first five minutes and the plot repeated three or four times so doomscrollers don't get lost.
Trump says he'll sue JPMorgan over 'debanking'
bullets.t: He said he'd sue within two weeks. JPMorgan says it doesn't close accounts over political beliefs.

bullets.h: Trump links Greenland push to not winning the Nobel Prize
bullets.t: In a message to Norway's prime minister he said he no longer felt an obligation to think purely of peace.

bullets.h: China's birthrate falls to its lowest since 1949
bullets.t: 5.63 births per 1,000 people, and the population fell for a fourth straight year.

bullets.h: Fashion designer Valentino dies at 93
bullets.t: The Italian designer behind 'Valentino red' launched his house in 1959.

bullets.h: Prince Harry puts the Daily Mail on trial
bullets.t: Harry, Elton John, and Elizabeth Hurley accuse the paper's publisher of unlawful information gathering. The trial runs about nine weeks.

bullets.h: A mini Sphere is headed to Washington
bullets.t: Planned for National Harbor, MD: 6,000 seats, about a third the size of Vegas, at $1 billion or more to build.

bullets.h: 23%: expected jump in data center construction spending this year
bullets.t: Offices, hotels, and warehouses are falling. Data centers would be over 6% of non-residential construction, up from 2% in 2023. The only limit may be finding enough workers.

bullets.h: Fortnight
bullets.t: Means 'a period of two weeks.'

issues.label: Issue of Jan 21
issues.top: Investors are officially afraid again

bullets.h: Good news: the sun sets at 5pm in New York tonight, and the next pre-5pm sunset isn't until November.
Investors are officially afraid again
bullets.t: Renewed tariff threats sparked a 'sell America' move. The Dow fell nearly 900 points, and the S&P 500 had its worst day since October.

bullets.h: Trump's Federal Reserve showdown is today
bullets.t: The Supreme Court hears his bid to fire Fed Gov. Lisa Cook. No president has ever removed a Fed governor.

bullets.h: Europe pushes back on Greenland threats
bullets.t: Macron at Davos: 'We prefer respect over bullies.'

bullets.h: Netflix upgrades its Warner Bros. Discovery offer to all cash
bullets.t: The offer is $82.7 billion, and Netflix also reported 325 million subscribers.

bullets.h: The Supreme Court did not rule on Trump's tariffs
bullets.t: No ruling yet. The next possible date is Feb. 20.

bullets.h: Davos can't stop talking about AI
bullets.t: The CEOs of Anthropic and Google DeepMind both expect AI to come for junior-level jobs. Satya Nadella said energy costs will decide the winner of the AI race, and Hassabis put Chinese AI about six months behind the West.

bullets.h: 750: UK chimney sweeps association members, up from about 590 in 2021
bullets.t: Energy prices are pushing Londoners back to wood stoves. Today's sweeps use CCTV instead of little boys.

bullets.h: Dickensian
bullets.t: Relating to living or working conditions below an acceptable standard, like in a Dickens novel.

issues.label: Issue of Jan 22
issues.top: Trump says Greenland deal is coming, tariffs off

bullets.h: The Razzie nominations are out, and the seven artificial dwarfs from Snow White are up for worst supporting actor.
SCOTUS seems poised to let Lisa Cook stay at the Fed
bullets.t: Justices across the spectrum worried that firing her would weaken the central bank's independence.

bullets.h: Jamie Dimon calls Trump's card fee cap an 'economic disaster'
bullets.t: He said a 10% cap would force a drastic reduction in credit cards.

bullets.h: Trump says Greenland deal is coming, tariffs off
bullets.t: He announced a 'framework' with NATO's Mark Rutte and dropped the promised tariffs, and markets rallied.

bullets.h: A massive winter storm is coming
bullets.t: Severe weather is expected to hit more than 200 million Americans across 2,000 miles from Friday.

bullets.h: Curtains come down on Sundance in Utah
bullets.t: After four decades in Park City, the festival moves to Boulder, CO next year. Boulder won with $34 million in tax credits over 10 years.

bullets.h: 11.2 billion: times the NYT's games were played last year
bullets.t: It just launched Crossplay, its first multiplayer game. Subscribers hit 12.33 million.

bullets.h: Dormant
bullets.t: Means 'temporarily inactive.'

issues.label: Issue of Jan 23
issues.top: Apple and OpenAI vie for AI gadgets

bullets.h: A huge winter storm is on the way from New Mexico to the East Coast, and airlines are already waiving change fees.
Trump sues JPMorgan and Jamie Dimon over 'debanking'
bullets.t: A $5 billion suit filed in Florida state court. JPMorgan says it has no merit.

bullets.h: Jack Smith testifies publicly about his Trump investigations
bullets.t: He told the House Judiciary Committee 'no one should be above the law.'

bullets.h: Free Solo, but live, comes to Netflix
bullets.t: Alex Honnold plans to climb the 1,667-foot Taipei 101 with no ropes. Weather pushed it back 24 hours.

bullets.h: Apple and OpenAI vie for AI gadgets
bullets.t: Apple may be building an AirTag-sized AI pin with cameras and microphones, possibly out by 2027. OpenAI says it is on track to show its first device in the second half of this year, built with Jony Ive and rumored to be screenless.

bullets.h: A Japanese toilet maker is an AI company now
bullets.t: Toto's stock jumped 11% after Goldman flagged its side business: chipmaking equipment that was 42% of operating income last year.

bullets.h: 16: Oscar nominations for Sinners, a record
bullets.t: It beat the old record of 14. One Battle After Another is still the favorite for best picture.

bullets.h: Harangued
bullets.t: Means 'lectured someone in an aggressive and critical manner.'

issues.label: Issue of Jan 24
issues.top: TikTok goes American

bullets.h: It's National Compliment Day. Beware the 'compliminsult,' like being told 'that's actually funny.'
Gold hits a record near $5,000 an ounce
bullets.t: Gold is up 8% on the week and 15% since Jan. 1. Silver topped $100 an ounce for the first time.

bullets.h: Baby, it's cold outside
bullets.t: At least 18 states and DC declared emergencies, and 8,300 flights were canceled for the weekend.

bullets.h: US, Russia, and Ukraine hold first trilateral peace talks
bullets.t: Held in the UAE, they are the first direct Russia-Ukraine talks since the 2022 invasion.

bullets.h: TikTok goes American
bullets.t: A $14 billion deal closed Thursday night. ByteDance keeps 19.9%, and Oracle, Silver Lake, and MGX split 45%. The app won't change much at first, but the new terms collect your precise location.

bullets.h: Former sideline reporter Michele Tafoya is running for Senate in Minnesota
A conspiracy theory says Earth loses gravity for seven seconds on Aug. 12
bullets.t: NASA says it won't.

bullets.h: Three Norwegian ski jumpers were suspended 18 months
bullets.t: They enlarged the crotches of their suits.

bullets.h: A cargo ship spill covered an English beach in raw french fries and onions
Atrocious
bullets.t: Means 'of a very poor quality; extremely bad or unpleasant.'

issues.label: Issue of Jan 27
issues.top: Social media is lowkey on trial

bullets.h: It's National Plan a Vacation Day, and research says planning a trip boosts happiness more than taking one.
Gold shatters its $5,000 record as investors seek safety
bullets.t: Gold briefly topped $5,100 and is up more than 80% in 12 months.

bullets.h: Michael Burry says he's buying GameStop
bullets.t: Last week GameStop's CEO bought 500,000 shares for about $21.5 million.

bullets.h: Saudi mega-development Neom will be scaled back
bullets.t: The $1.5 trillion project is being downsized. The Line, a planned self-sustaining city, could become a data center hub.

bullets.h: Social media is lowkey on trial
bullets.t: Jury selection began in Los Angeles in a landmark case accusing Meta, TikTok, and YouTube of causing social media addiction in kids. Snap settled, and 5,000+ similar lawsuits are pending. A WSJ poll found 71% support banning most social media for under-16s.

bullets.h: $3.75: price of the new California Post print edition
bullets.t: Rupert Murdoch's newest tabloid launched with a newsroom of about 80 to 100. Its first front page: 'Oscar Wild.'

bullets.h: Unwieldy
bullets.t: Means 'difficult to manage.'

issues.label: Issue of Jan 28
issues.top: EU and India clinch 'the mother of all deals'

bullets.h: A $100 million gift means every US Olympian and Paralympian gets $200,000, so the last-place curler in Milan earns the same as the top hockey scorer.
US consumer confidence falls to its lowest since 2014
bullets.t: The Conference Board's gauge dropped to 84.5, with gas and grocery costs the most-cited worries.

bullets.h: EU and India clinch 'the mother of all deals'
bullets.t: After about 20 years of talks, the deal cuts or removes duties on 90% of the $136 billion in goods traded. India will slash tariffs on European cars from as high as 110% to as low as 10%.

bullets.h: Early issues for TikTok US
bullets.t: In the first five days after the deal closed, app deletions climbed 150%. Users reacted to a new privacy pop-up and reports of blocked videos. TikTok blamed a data center outage, and California's governor announced a probe.

bullets.h: Pinterest lays off 15% of employees to pivot to AI
bullets.t: About 675 of its 4,500 workers are out. AI was cited for nearly 55,000 US layoffs last year.

bullets.h: 85 seconds: the Doomsday Clock's distance from midnight
bullets.t: The closest it has ever been. The Bulletin's chair says AI is supercharging misinformation.

bullets.h: Nigh
bullets.t: Means 'near.'

issues.label: Issue of Jan 29
issues.top: Fed holds steady in first rate decision of the year

bullets.h: Southwest has scrapped its 54-year-old open seating policy. Future generations will never know the pain of the back-row middle seat.
Fed holds steady in its first rate decision of the year
bullets.t: Rates stay at 3.5% to 3.75%, the first pause since July after three cuts. Waller and Miran dissented in favor of a cut.

bullets.h: Amazon lays off 16,000 employees
bullets.t: That's 30,000 corporate jobs cut since October, about 10% of its white-collar workforce.

bullets.h: Trump warns Iran its 'time is running out' for a nuclear deal
bullets.t: He said a massive armada is headed toward Iran.

bullets.h: Tesla has its first annual revenue drop
bullets.t: Revenue slipped 3% to $94.8 billion and Q4 profit fell 61%. Tesla plans to invest $2 billion in xAI and stop making the Model S and Model X to build Optimus robots.

bullets.h: Revenue and AI spending grow at Meta and Microsoft
bullets.t: Meta posted record Q4 sales of $59.9 billion and plans up to $135 billion in 2026 capital spending, and its stock rose. Microsoft's capex is up 66%, and its stock fell.

bullets.h: The risky AI assistant clawing its way to viral fame
bullets.t: Moltbot, an open-source assistant built on Claude, is blowing up on GitHub. It runs on your own machine, which leaves you open to prompt injection attacks, so run it on a separate computer.

bullets.h: 4%: Starbucks US same-store sales growth, the first rise since 2023
bullets.t: Revenue rose 5% to $9.9 billion, but profit fell more than 60%.

bullets.h: Forage
bullets.t: Means 'to wander in search of food.'

issues.label: Issue of Jan 30
issues.top: Why the value of the US dollar is shedding cents

bullets.h: It's a winter Friday: skip the gym, watch a bad Fast & Furious movie, and Google 'Bahamas wi-fi good?' at 2am.
Why the US dollar is shedding cents
bullets.t: Down 2% this year and almost 11% over the past year. Gold and the Swiss franc are surging at the same time, a sign the dollar may be losing its safe-haven status.

bullets.h: Trump says he'll name his Fed Chair pick today
bullets.t: Former Fed Gov. Kevin Warsh was a 95% favorite on Polymarket.

bullets.h: Melania set to lose a lot of money at the box office
bullets.t: The documentary is expected to earn about $3 million opening weekend against $75 million Amazon spent.

bullets.h: Apple revenue soars on 'staggering' iPhone demand
bullets.t: Revenue grew 16% to about $144 billion, and Tim Cook said 2.5 billion Apple devices are now in use.

bullets.h: Why the market is punishing Microsoft but not Meta
bullets.t: Microsoft fell nearly 10%, erasing $350+ billion, while Meta climbed 10%. Nearly half of Microsoft's contracted future revenue depends on OpenAI.

bullets.h: $10 million: top price for a 30-second Super Bowl ad
bullets.t: The average is $8 million, and nearly 40% of advertisers are new this year.

bullets.h: Beaucoup
bullets.t: French for 'a lot.'

issues.label: Issue of Jan 31
issues.top: We have a Fed chair nominee

bullets.h: Sony is making four Beatles movies, one from each band member's perspective, and they won't hit theaters until April 2028.
We have a Fed chair nominee
bullets.t: Trump nominated former Fed Gov. Kevin Warsh to replace Powell. Gold dropped as much as 12% and silver as much as 36% while the dollar soared.

bullets.h: The DOJ released 3+ million pages of Epstein documents
bullets.t: The final release includes more than 3 million pages, 2,000 videos, and 180,000 images.

bullets.h: Actress Catherine O'Hara has died at age 71
bullets.t: Known for Schitt's Creek, Home Alone, and Beetlejuice.

bullets.h: Musk may combine his companies
bullets.t: Reuters says Musk may merge SpaceX with xAI, and Bloomberg says he may merge it with Tesla instead. SpaceX is heading toward a record $50 billion IPO as early as June.

bullets.h: Neil Young gave Greenland residents a year of his music and films
Bryan Johnson picked a fight with the AG1 supplement over its clinical trial
Bridgit Mendler's satellite startup landed a $50 million government contract
Facebook conspiracy theorists claim a 'Leviathan is waking up near Virginia'
bullets.t: The screenshot was doctored.

bullets.h: Terraforming
bullets.t: Means 'transforming a planet so it is suitable for human life.'
